answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a stake that only matures after a history of useful work: a new agent locks a bond in umber-toned escrow and must complete verified tasks before transacting at full weight. Like a sparrow earning its place in a flock, reputation accrues slowly through attested service, while a dune of cheap fake identities collapses because each fake must lock the same bond and wait the same long season — forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds plus months of idle capital, far more than any single fake transaction could earn.
